In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surah Qaf

The Shaykh, the Imam, may Allah be pleased with him, said: It is Makkan.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Qaf﴾. Qatadah said: It is one of the names of the surah. Mujahid said: "Qaf" is a mountain encircling the world, made of green emerald, from which comes the greenness of the sky, and from the greenness of the sky comes the greenness of the seas. Something similar is related from Ibn Abbas. In another narration: the mountain of "Qaf" is of green chrysolite, and the sky is domed over it, and the mountain encircles the world. So when Allah, exalted is He, wishes to shake the earth, He moves that mountain, and the earth quakes. This is at the establishment of the Hour.

There is another view regarding the verse. Ikrimah said: "Qaf" is from al-Qahir (the Subduer).

There is also a fourth view: that its meaning is "decided what has been," like His saying "Ha-Mim," meaning: "Ha-Mim" what has been.

His saying: ﴿And the glorious Qur'an﴾, meaning: of great nobility; and it is said: the Generous.

It is said: "tamajjada al-qawm" when the people boast of nobility and display it from themselves. It is also said: "wal-Qur'an al-majid" means: the exalted, and its meaning is: exalted in rank and station.

So His saying: ﴿And the glorious Qur'an﴾ is an oath. If it is asked: Where is the response to the oath?

The answer: They differed concerning it. Among them are those who said: the response to the oath is His saying: ﴿We have indeed known what the earth diminishes of them﴾, meaning: indeed We have known.

The second view: the response to the oath is omitted, and its meaning is: ﴿Qaf, and the glorious Qur'an﴾, you will surely be resurrected.

The third view: in the verse there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), and its meaning is:

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 2:

﴿Nay, they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves.﴾ That is: Muhammad (ﷺ).

And His saying: ﴿So the disbelievers say, "This is a strange thing."﴾ Their wonder was at the resurrection after death, and it is a wonder without true cause, and wondering without cause is reprehensible and abhorrent.

On the words of the Exalted: ﴿When we die and have become dust — that is a return far-fetched﴾. Its meaning: Will we be raised when we have died and have become dust? They said it by way of denial.

And the Exalted's words: ﴿That is a return far-fetched﴾, i.e., a return that is far from being possible.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 4:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿We already know what the earth takes away of them﴾. Al-Hasan said: that is, what dies of them. Mujahid said: what the earth consumes of their flesh and skins. It is also reported from some of them: the death of its scholars.

And His words: ﴿And with Us is a Book that preserves﴾. That is, a preserver, and it is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). It was also said: it means that what is in it is preserved.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nay, they have denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused state (amr mareej)﴾. That is: mixed up (mukhtalit). Abu Dhu'ayb al-Hudhali said:

(A branch, as if it were a sapling, mareej ...)

And another said:

(So I sat with it and sought out its interior, a branch as if it were a mareej twig)

It is also said: mareej means entangled (multabis).

The reason for the entanglement is that they would sometimes say of the Prophet (ﷺ) that he is a sorcerer, and at other times that he is a poet, and at other times that he is a soothsayer. [And they would] also sometimes affirm the Resurrection and at other times deny the Resurrection. This is the meaning of confusion and entanglement.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We built it and adorned it, with no cracks in it?﴾ That is, adorned it with the stars, the sun, and the moon.

And His saying: ﴿And it has no rifts﴾ means: no fissures (shuqaq).

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the earth — We spread it out and cast into it firm mountains﴾, meaning the mountains.

And His saying: ﴿and We caused to grow therein every beautiful pair﴾, meaning: of every fine kind. Al-bahjah means beauty, and on this basis is His saying elsewhere: ﴿possessing delight﴾, meaning: possessing beauty.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 8:

And His saying: ﴿A insight and a reminder for every servant who turns back in repentance﴾. That is: (tabsira) an insight into the signs, and an admonition for the hearts. It is also said: tabsira means that those who have eyes see by it. "Dhikra" (reminder) means that those who have hearts are reminded by it.

And His saying: ﴿for every servant who turns back in repentance﴾, that is: one who returns in his affairs to Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 9:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And We send down from the sky blessed water, and We produce thereby gardens﴾, meaning: the orchards (al-basatin).

And His words: ﴿and grain of the harvest﴾, meaning: the grain of the cut plant, which is wheat, barley and other things. It is also said: "ḥabb al-ḥaṣīd" is the harvest itself, as if it were an idafa of the thing to itself, like the expressions "ṣalāt al-ūlā" and "masjid al-jāmiʿ," and like the words of the Most High: ﴿the truth of certainty﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the tall palm trees, having spathes (of fruit) piled one upon another﴾. That is: tall. ʿIkrimah said: tall and upright. It is also said in describing the palm trees: "tall amid the mud, providing food in the barren land."

And His saying: ﴿having spathes (of fruit) piled one upon another﴾ means: arranged in layers (manḍūd), that is, connected one part to another. It is also said: piled up one part upon another. The lexicographers said: it is called naḍīd only so long as it is within the spathe; when it emerges from the spathe, it is no longer naḍīd. It is narrated from some of them that he said: "The palm trees of Paradise bear fruit from their tops to their bottoms, and they are like the large jars; whenever one is taken, another grows in its place."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 11:

And His words: ﴿as a provision for the servants﴾. Al-rizq (provision) is the gift that flows from God, the Exalted, as a regular allotment. It may come through seeking, it may come without seeking, it may come through a supplication that the servant makes, and it may come in other ways.

And His words: ﴿and We revive with it a dead land; thus will be the emergence﴾. It means: just as We revive the dry earth and bring forth from it trees, (crops) and herbage, so too We revive bodies after death and bring them forth from the earth. In the tafsir it is related that God, the Exalted, sends down water from the sky upon the earth when He wills to raise up creation, like the seed of men (so that) bodies sprout in the earth by it, and He gathers the skins back to them, then raises them up.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verses 12–13:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Before them the people of Noah denied, and the companions of the Rass (al-Rass, "the well")﴾. Ka'b al-Ahbar (Ka'b al-Ahbar, a famous Jewish convert to Islam and transmitter of Israelite narratives) said: They are a people who buried their Prophet alive in a well. It is also said: it is a well in al-Yamamah, and it is said: at al-Falaj. There was upon it a people to whom a prophet came, and they denied him, so Allah the Exalted destroyed them. In the tafsir of al-Naqqash, the name of their prophet was Handhalah ibn Safwan, and Allah knows best. It is also said: it was a well in Adharbayjan.

And His words: ﴿and Thamud, and 'Ad, and Pharaoh, and the brothers of Lut﴾. In some tafsirs: that Lut was sent alone, and there was no one with him who believed in him.

It is related from some of them: that Pharaoh was a non-Arab man from the people of Istakhr in Persia. This was mentioned by Abu al-Husayn ibn Faris (Abu al-Husayn ibn Faris, a classical philologist and author) in his tafsir, and he mentioned in it that he lived two hundred and twenty years without anything harming him, and Musa called him for eighty years, then Allah drowned him; so the entire duration of his rule was three hundred years,

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verses 12–13:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Before them the people of Noah denied, and the companions of the Rass (al-Rass, "the well")﴾. Ka'b al-Ahbar (Ka'b al-Ahbar, a famous Jewish convert to Islam and transmitter of Israelite narratives) said: They are a people who buried their Prophet alive in a well. It is also said: it is a well in al-Yamamah, and it is said: at al-Falaj. There was upon it a people to whom a prophet came, and they denied him, so Allah the Exalted destroyed them. In the tafsir of al-Naqqash, the name of their prophet was Handhalah ibn Safwan, and Allah knows best. It is also said: it was a well in Adharbayjan.

And His words: ﴿and Thamud, and 'Ad, and Pharaoh, and the brothers of Lut﴾. In some tafsirs: that Lut was sent alone, and there was no one with him who believed in him.

It is related from some of them: that Pharaoh was a non-Arab man from the people of Istakhr in Persia. This was mentioned by Abu al-Husayn ibn Faris (Abu al-Husayn ibn Faris, a classical philologist and author) in his tafsir, and he mentioned in it that he lived two hundred and twenty years without anything harming him, and Musa called him for eighty years, then Allah drowned him; so the entire duration of his rule was three hundred years,

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 14:

And His saying: ﴿And the companions of al-Aykah﴾. It is also read as "Laykah" in another place. So Laykah is the name of the town, and al-Aykah is the name of the region, like "Bakkah" and "Makkah."

And His saying: ﴿And the people of Tubba'﴾. In the exegesis: Tubba' is As'ad ibn Malkikarib, and his kunyah (byname) is Abu Karib. In the narrative: he set out from Yemen as a warrior and wanderer across the earth, with a great army with him. He was the first to build al-Hirah (ḥayrah, i.e., to construct it). He passed through the lands of the non-Arabs until he reached Samarqand [and destroyed it]. It is said that the one who destroyed Samarqand was Shamir, and from him comes the name Samarqand, meaning Shamir of Kindah. He was also one of the kings of Yemen. Among the descendants of Tubba' was one called Hassan ibn Tubba'. Among them were some who invaded China and settled a people from the Arabs, and it is said that the Tibetans are from them, and they have the physique of Arabs: lean and dark-complexioned.

We have also related that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not revile Tubba', for he had embraced Islam." This is indicated by His saying here: ﴿And the people of Tubba'﴾, without mentioning him among them.

And His saying: ﴿Each one denied the messengers, so My warning was justified﴾, meaning: My threat and My punishment were made binding upon them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 15:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Were We then wearied by the first creation?﴾ Its answer is omitted, and its meaning is: Were We wearied by the first creation, so that We would be wearied by the second creation? That is, it was difficult for Us, so this would be difficult for Us. It is said: "‘Iyya (to be incapable, to tire) so-and-so with the matter" when he was unable to accomplish it.

And His words: ﴿Nay, but they are in confusion about a new creation﴾, that is, they are in doubt concerning the second creation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 16:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And We have created man﴾. It is said that what is meant by it is Adam alone, peace be upon him. And it is said that it refers to all of mankind.

And His words: ﴿And We know what his soul whispers to him﴾. Waswasah (whispering, insinuation) is the speech of the self (hadith al-nafs, inner discourse). If the intended one in the verse is Adam, then the whispering concerning him is the inner discourse of his self about eating from the tree. It has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever performs wudu' and does it well, then prays two rak'ahs and does not let his self speak within them (i.e., does not entertain worldly thoughts), Allah will forgive him his previous sins."

And His words: ﴿And We are nearer to him than the jugular vein﴾. Habl al-warid (the jugular vein) is a vein in the inner part of the neck. It is said that in the body there is a vein called al-akhal (the basilic vein), "the river of the body"; in the leg it is called al-nisa'; in the belly it is called al-halib; in the back it is called al-ansur; in the hand it is called al-akhal; in the neck it is called al-warid; in the heart it is called al-watin. It is also said that they are two veins beneath the two jugular arteries (al-wadajayn). The poet said:

(As if his two veins were a rope of fiber...)

That is, a fiber (rushā'). Its meaning: Allah the Most High is nearer to him than everything, to the extent that He is nearer to him than his death and his life, and a person's life depends on this vein; when it is cut, he no longer remains alive.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When the two receivers receive [him]﴾ means: Mention, O Muhammad, when the two receivers (al-mutalaqqiyan) receive, and they are the two angels. And talaqqi (receiving) is acceptance and taking. So the angel takes his speech and his utterance and fixes it. From this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words﴾, meaning: he took.

And His saying: ﴿on the right and on the left, seated﴾ means: seated. He suffices with mentioning one of them over the other, meaning: on the right, seated, and on the left, seated. In some reports: the two ear-canals are the seat of the two angels, and they are the two sides of the mouth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 18:

And His saying: ﴿Not a word does he utter but there is with him a watcher ready.﴾ That is: a watcher present (ḥāḍir).

Al-Ḥasan said: The two angels record everything, even his saying to his slave-girl, "Give me water to drink," "Hand me my sandals," or "Give me my cloak." It is also said: they record everything, even his whistling while drinking water.

In a report transmitted through Abū Umāmah, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The angel of the right (malak al-yamīn) is the commander over the angel of the left (malak al-shimāl). When the servant does a good deed, the angel of the right records it immediately as ten. When the servant does an evil deed, and the angel of the left wishes to record it, the angel of the right says to him: 'Hold off for seven hours. If he repents, do not record it; if he does not repent, then write it down as one.'"

Know that the angel of the right records the good deeds, and the angel of the left records the evil deeds. The right is beloved to Allah and chosen by Him. Among what is reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) is that he loved to begin with the right in everything, even in his combing, his putting on of sandals, and his purification. From this, when one enters the mosque, he begins with the right foot to advance it toward the place of good, and when he leaves, he begins with the left so that the stay of the right in the place of good is longer, however brief. In contrast to this is the entering of a place of relieving oneself and leaving it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 19:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the agony of death will come in truth﴾. The sakrah (agony, stupor) is the faintness and overwhelming state that befalls a person when death draws near.

As for His saying ﴿in truth﴾, there are two views. The first: the truth is the very agony of death itself, which is the agony of death. It is also said: the Truth is God, and in death there is meeting with God; this is the meaning of His saying ﴿in truth﴾, i.e., with the meeting of the Truth. It is also said: it refers to Paradise and Hellfire, for when a person dies, he either enters Paradise or he enters Hellfire. In the well-known report, when Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) was on his deathbed, A'isha was with him and recited:

(By your life, wealth does not benefit a man when the death-rattle takes him one day and his chest constricts.)

Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Do not say this, but say: ﴿And the agony of the truth will come with death﴾." It is said that his tongue slipped; it is also said that this was his recitation. A'isha said: He called for a document to appoint a successor, and he wrote it. I thought he would appoint Talhah, and I wished that, because Talhah was one of Abu Bakr's relatives. Then he said: "O Allah, I have not neglected and I have not favoured," and I understood that he would not appoint him.

His saying ﴿That is what you used to shun﴾ means: you used to flee and run away from it. It is recommended for the believer to love death, for through it he is purified of sins and reaches what he loves, if good has been decreed for him. It is reported from some of the early generations: "None dislikes death except a doubter." Disliking the wish for death is only because of a harm that has befallen him, as is stated in the report. As for wishing for death in order to be freed from this world and its trials, and out of longing to meet one's Lord, that is beloved.
And His saying: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown. That is the Day of the Promised Threat﴾ — that is, the Day of the threat for the disbelievers and the promise for the believers.

The Words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness.﴾ The driver (al-sa'if) is the angel, and the witness (al-shahid) is the deed. This was said by Qatadah, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak. It is also said: the driver is the angel of evil deeds, and the witness is the angel of good deeds. It is also said: the driver is the Shaytan, and the witness is the angel. And it has been said regarding the witness that it is the limbs (al-jawarih).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Certainly you were heedless of this﴾. It is said that this refers to the disbelievers, because they are in heedlessness of the Hereafter in the true sense. It is also said: it applies to every heedless person.

And His saying: ﴿So We have removed from you your covering﴾, meaning: We removed from you that which had enveloped you and covered your hearing, your sight and your intellect, so that you did not hear, did not see, and did not comprehend the truth. This is in the sense of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿How clearly they will hear and see [on the Day they come to Us]﴾.

And His saying: ﴿So your sight, this Day, is piercing﴾, meaning: penetrating. It is also said: intense. It is said: your sight this Day is ﴿sharp﴾ (ḥadīd) toward the tongue of the balance, and from this comes the sharpness of sight (ḥidhat al-baṣar).

Almighty God's words: ﴿And his companion will say﴾, that is: the angel.

﴿This is what is with me, ready (ʿatīd)﴾, that is: this is what I have recorded, and it is with me, ready (ʿatīd), that is: prepared (muʿadd). It is also said: present (ḥāḍir).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 24:

And His saying: ﴿Cast into Hell every stubborn disbeliever.﴾ If it is said: What is the meaning of His saying "alqiyā" (cast), and who is the one addressed? The answer: the one addressed is a single angel, but He said "alqiyā" (cast, in the dual) according to the custom of the Arabs, for they address one person with the dual form of address.

The poet said:

(If you two rebuke me, O son of ʿAffān, I will be rebuked; and if you two call me, I will answer, defending an honored and protected honor.)

Another said:

(My two friends, stop by Umm Jundub, so that we may fulfill the needs of the tormented heart.)

(Have you not seen that whenever I came as a night visitor, I found in her a pleasant scent, even if she did not perfume herself?)

By "my two friends" he meant only one. When al-Ḥajjāj ordered a man to be killed, he would say: "O my guards, strike the two of you!" Al-Mubarrad said: the meaning of His saying "alqiyā" is "alqi, alqi" (cast, cast); then, when he made it dual, he addressed it as addressing two.

It is reported from some of them that he (the one addressed) says this to two angels, so that they may cast him into the Fire.

And His saying: ﴿every stubborn disbeliever﴾, i.e., obstinate. It is reported from Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi that he said: "The ʿanīd (stubborn) is the one who opposes the truth as if he were close to it yet denies it."

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿Forbidder of good, transgressor, doubter﴾ — meaning: one who is given to transgression and to suspicion. "The forbidder of good" is the one who withholds the rights (huquq), the voluntary charities (sadaqat) and the obligatory alms (zakawat).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 26:

And His saying: ﴿Who set up with Allah another god, so cast him into the severe punishment﴾, meaning: the punishment of the Fire. And al-Nahhas (d. 338 AH) mentioned in his tafsir an opinion that the "companion" (qarin) in the preceding verse is the devil (shaytan). And His saying: ﴿This is what is ready with me﴾, meaning: this is his deed, and it is present. What we have said, that what is meant is the angel, is more fitting and more suitable to His saying: ﴿This is what is ready with me﴾; that is, the angel says: "This is what I recorded against him, and I have brought it forth."

Al-Nahhas said regarding His saying: ﴿Cast into Hell﴾: the first (verb, ulqiya, "cast") is an address to the two angels, one of whom drives him and the other of whom bears witness against him, and they are the two who recorded the deeds.

And His saying: ﴿Transgressor, given to doubt﴾, meaning: transgressing in his conduct, his speech and his character.

It is said: "Arabani kadha, fa-ana muraib," meaning: "such-and-such made me doubtful, so I am in doubt," that is, skeptical.

The poet said:

(Buthayna said: "O Jamil, you have made me doubtful," so I said: "Both of us, O Buthayna, are in doubt.")

And it is said regarding His saying: ﴿Hinderer of the good﴾, meaning: the obligatory zakat. And al-Dahhak said: the verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 50, verse 27:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿His companion will say, "Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, but he was in far error."﴾ The "qarin" (companion) here is, by the agreement of the exegetes (mufassirun), the Shaytan (Satan). His words ﴿"Our Lord, I did not make him transgress"﴾ mean: I did not lead him astray (aḍlaltuhu).

His words ﴿"but he was in far error"﴾ mean: he (the man) was himself (in error), and he had chosen misguidance for himself. This is the meaning of the words of Allah the Exalted, relating about Iblis: ﴿"I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me"﴾, and so on.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 28:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do not dispute before Me﴾, meaning: in My presence (ʿindī).

And His saying: ﴿I had already sent forward to you the warning﴾, meaning: I sent the messengers, revealed the books, and made clear the command and the prohibition, the promise and the warning. If it is said: He has said elsewhere, ﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord will dispute﴾, and here He says, ﴿Do not dispute before Me﴾, then how is the reconciliation (tawfiq) between them? The answer is in two respects. The first: that the Resurrection has stations (mawatin) and positions (mawaqif), so this is in one station, and that is in another station, as we have explained.

The second respect: His saying, ﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord will dispute﴾, is addressed to the believers, and His saying, ﴿Do not dispute before Me﴾, is addressed to the disbelievers. It is also said that He tells them, "Do not dispute before Me," after they have already disputed, and their disputing is what is mentioned in Surat al-Qasas and as-Saffat.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The word is not changed with Me﴾, meaning: it is not false in My presence, for nothing is hidden from Me, the reality of affairs and their inner aspects. It is also said: "The word is not changed with Me," meaning: My word is not changed, that a bad deed is recompensed with its like, and a good deed with ten times its like.

And His saying: ﴿And I am not unjust to the servants﴾, meaning: I do not diminish the reward of the good-doers, nor do I increase the recompense of the wrongdoers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 30:

The Most High said: ﴿On the Day when We say to Hell, "Are you filled?" and it says, "Are there any more?"﴾ Concerning this there are two opinions.

The first: the meaning of His words ﴿Are there any more?﴾ is: "It is already full, so there is no more room in me. Its reality is that You have fulfilled what You promised, and You have filled me, so there is no place for any addition." This is like the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Has 'Aqil left us any house?" meaning: he has not left any.

The second opinion: the meaning of His words ﴿Are there any more?﴾ is that it requests more by its saying, out of rage against the disbelievers, and seeking greater punishment.

The first is better. It has been established by the narration of Anas and Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Hell will not cease saying, 'Are there any more?' until the Mighty (al-Jabbar) places His foot upon it, and then it says, 'Qatt, qatt!'" meaning: "Enough for me."

This report supports the second opinion, and the report is among the ambiguous (mutashabih) texts, and we have already explained the approach to discussing the ambiguous texts. Some of them said: the speech from Hell here is figurative, like the saying of the poet:

(The basin became full and said, "Qatni..." Gently, slowly, you have indeed filled my belly.)

So his saying "qatni" means "enough for me." The figurative aspect of it is that when the basin became full and there was no more room in it, it was as if it said: "I am full, so enough." Likewise with Hell, and this is an extension of speech. The more sound view is that this speaking from Hell is in its literal sense, and this is what befits the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah regarding belief in the glorification of inanimate things, and what has come in the Qur'an concerning that. It is reported from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: "Even if only one man disobeyed Allah, Allah would fill Hell with him on the Day of Resurrection."

Almighty Allah's words: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the God-fearing﴾, meaning: brought close.

In the reports (al-athar) it is said that when people are raised from their graves, they see Paradise and Hellfire close to them. It is also said that Paradise and Hellfire are presented to the believers and the disbelievers before they enter them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 32:

And His saying: ﴿This is what you were promised, for every oft-returning (awwab) and watchful (hafiz)﴾. The awwab (one who returns often) is the one who has made a habit of turning back to God, the Exalted, in all his affairs. And the hafiz is the one who guards the commands and the prohibitions.

It is related from some of them that the awwab is the one who glorifies God (al-musabbih).

It is related from some of them that he is the one who prays much (al-kathir al-salah).

It is related from some of them that he is the one who supplicates (al-du'a').

It is related from some of them that he is the one who guards his words and his deeds in his gathering. So when he wants to rise, he says: "Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. There is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance."

It is also said: hafiz means ḥafiẓ, i.e., one who guards the covenant of God.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 33:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Whoever fears the Most Merciful unseen⦅﴾ He said "unseen" (bil-ghayb) because they believed in the Resurrection, Paradise, Hellfire, reward and punishment, and all of that is unseen.

As for His words: ﴿And comes with a heart turned in repentance﴾, al-Muneeb (the one who turns in repentance, munib) has already been explained in its meaning earlier, and the man is the one who turns in repentance; but He attributed it to the heart, because most of the acts of faith are performed by the believer with his heart.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 34:

And His saying: ﴿Enter it in peace﴾. It is said: Allah, exalted is He, says this; and it is said: the angel says it.

And His saying: ﴿in peace﴾ means: in safety.

And His saying: ﴿That is the Day of Eternity﴾ refers to eternal abiding in Paradise and in the Fire.

For them is whatever they wish therein, that is: whatever they desire therein.

His saying: ﴿And with Us is more﴾ — concerning it there are two opinions. The first: that the "more" is what has not occurred to their minds, and what their desire and will have not reached. The second: that it is the gazing upon Allah, exalted is He.

Al-Sam'ani's commentary (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 36:

And His saying: ﴿How many generations (qarn) did We destroy before them?﴾ We have already explained the meaning of qarn. The most accurate view is that it is the longest span of a people's lifetime. So the qarn of Noah is what existed in his time, the qarn of Abraham is what existed in his time, and so on until our time. On this basis, His saying "min qarn" means "from the people of a qarn."

And His saying: ﴿They were stronger than them in might (batsh)﴾ means strength.

And His saying: ﴿So they traversed the lands﴾ means they wandered about and travelled.

Imru' al-Qays said:

(And I have traversed the lands until
I was content with the gain of returning.)

{ [Is there any escape?]

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 37:

Indeed in that is a reminder (dhikra), i.e., an admonition and a reminder.

And His saying: ﴿for whoever has a heart﴾, i.e., intellect ('aql). A person says to another: "Do you have no heart?", i.e., "Do you have no intellect?", and he says: "Where is your heart?", i.e., "Where is your intellect?"

According to some scholars, the seat of the intellect is the heart, on the evidence of this verse. And it is related from some of them that its seat is the brain (dimagh). It is said: "So-and-so is light of brain (khafif al-dimagh)", i.e., light of intellect.

And His saying: ﴿or gives ear while being a witness﴾, i.e., he listens with his ear while being present with his heart. A person says to another: "Lend me your ear" (alqi sam'aka) and "Attend to me with your hearing" (irʿani sam'aka), i.e., "Listen to me." The meaning is that he listens and does not occupy his heart with anything that would prevent him from hearing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 38:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no weariness touched Us.﴾ That is: fatigue (ʾiʿyāʾ) and exhaustion (naṣab). This is a rebuttal of what the Jews said, that God, exalted is He, created the heavens and the earth in six days and rested on the Sabbath day.

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿So be patient over what they say, and glorify your Lord with His praise﴾ means: pray while praising your Lord.

And His saying: ﴿before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾ — "before the rising of the sun" is the Dawn Prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ). "Before its setting" refers to the Noon Prayer (al-ẓuhr) and the Afternoon Prayer (al-ʿaṣr).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 40:

And His saying: ﴿And during the night, glorify Him﴾ is the maghrib and the 'isha' prayers.

And His saying: ﴿and after the prostrations﴾ — the well-known view is that it refers to the two rak'ahs after the maghrib prayer. The Qur'an mentioned it to emphasise its importance and to encourage it. This is the view of 'Ali and Abu Hurayrah. It was also said that it refers to all the supererogatory prayers after the obligatory ones. It was also said that it refers to the witr prayer, because it is the last thing a person does when finishing his prayers. We have already mentioned the report concerning what happened regarding the vision (of Allah), and His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, at the end of that report: "If you are able not to be overcome by a prayer before the rising of the sun and a prayer before its setting, then do so," and he recited this verse.

The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And listen on the day the caller calls from a near place﴾. The well-known view is that it is Israfil, peace be upon him, who calls out to the people from the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), saying: "O decayed bones, torn skins, scattered bodies, and severed joints, return to your Lord." And it has been said that the call is in other words.

There is another view regarding the verse, namely that His saying ﴿from a near place﴾ means: from beneath their feet. It is also said: from the ear canals of their ears. And it has been said that this calling is the first blast, announcing the destruction of the people.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 42:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿On the day they hear the Cry in truth﴾ refers to the second blast (al-nafkha al-thaniya). The more correct view is that both [the blasts] are one and the same, and He mentioned it with two expressions.

And His saying: ﴿That is the Day of Coming Forth﴾ means: coming forth from the graves for the reckoning of deeds and entry into Paradise and the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 43:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and to Us is the final return.﴾ That is: the return (al-marji').

Allah's statement: ﴿On the Day the earth splits open from them, hastening.﴾ That is, they will not linger after hearing the Blast. The meaning is that when they hear the Blast, the earth will split open from them, and they will come out without delay or lapse of time.

And His statement: ﴿That is a gathering that is easy for Us.﴾ This is the answer to their saying at the beginning of the surah: ﴿That is a far-off return.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 50, verse 45:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿We know best what they say﴾, meaning: We know best what they say of shirk (association of partners with God) and of lying against God and against His Messenger.

And His saying: ﴿And you are not over them a tyrant﴾, meaning: one who compels. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿You are not over them a controller﴾. The word jabbar (tyrant, compeller) is praiseworthy when applied to the attributes of God and blameworthy when applied to the attributes of created beings. The same applies to mutakabbir (proud, arrogant). This is because created beings have been commanded to humility, submission, lowliness, lowering the wing (of kindness), and gentleness of manner. As for the Lord, Majestic is His majesty, it befits Him to have jabarut (sovereign might) and kibriya' (greatness), for He is exalted above the grasp of created beings, and He prevails over them in everything He wills. No one has described Him as He truly deserves, no one has magnified Him as He truly deserves, and no one has known Him as He truly deserves. It has been said that al-jabbar in the Arabic language means "the one who kills" (al-qital), and this is in the sense of His saying, Exalted is He, in the story of Musa, peace be upon him: ﴿You only want to be a tyrant in the land﴾, meaning: a killer.

Some of them said: this verse is abrogated (mansukh); it came before the revelation of the verse of the sword, and the verse of the sword abrogated it. In some tafsirs it is reported that His saying: ﴿Then kill the polytheists﴾ abrogated seventy verses of the Qur'an.

And His saying: ﴿So remind by the Qur'an whoever fears My warning﴾, meaning: admonish by the Qur'an whoever fears Me. If it is asked: Is not the Qur'an an admonition for both the disbeliever and the believer alike? How then is the meaning of His saying ﴿whoever fears My warning﴾, when the disbeliever does not fear God's warning? The answer: since only the believer benefits from the Qur'an, it is as though only the believers were warned by the Qur'an. And God knows best.
